title: Completed coefficient-first compactification projection coordinates
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Use the ordinary derived categories $D_T$ of modules over the completed coefficient ring on each small pro-etale site, with the ordinary pullback $f_R^*$ and representative-normalized ordinary tensor $\otimes^o$ of [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge], the completed pullback $\widehat f^*$ and completed tensor $\widehat\otimes$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and the normalized compactification model $m$ and actual proper/open image $P_c=Rp_{*,R}j_{!,R}$ of [def-pur-compactification-reduction-models]. The categories and coefficient presentations are those of [def-sp-projection-reduction-presentation]. Let $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow Z,p:Z\to Y)$ be a compactification of $f:X\to Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and take arbitrary $K\in D_Y$ and $M\in D_X$.

Define the coefficient-first ordinary endpoints $I^o=f_R^*K\otimes^o M$ and $S^o=K\otimes^o P_cM$, and their completed endpoints $I^c=\widehat f^*K\widehat\otimes M$ and $S^c=K\widehat\otimes P_cM$. Write $\chi_T$ for the specified ordinary-to-completed tensor augmentation and $\eta_f:f_R^*\to\widehat f^*$ for the specified pullback augmentation in $m$. Define $u_I:I^o\to I^c$ to be $\chi_X$ followed by $\eta_f(K)\widehat\otimes\mathrm{id}_M$, and $u_S:S^o\to S^c$ to be $\chi_Y(K,P_cM)$. Use the signed symmetry $\tau$ induced by the actual ordinary tensor representative model [def-pur-ringed-site-signed-tensor-models]. With the actual proper-counit/open-unit projection $\pi^o:P_cM\otimes^o K\to P_c(M\otimes^o f_R^*K)$ of [def-pur-integral-ringed-projection-maps], define the coefficient-first projection $\alpha^o=P_c(\tau)\circ\pi^o\circ\tau:S^o\to P_cI^o$. Finally, for specified isomorphisms $v:S^o\xrightarrow\sim S^c$ and $h:I^o\xrightarrow\sim I^c$, define $\alpha_{v,h}=P_c(h)\circ\alpha^o\circ v^{-1}:S^c\to P_cI^c$. In the canonical completed coordinates use $v=\operatorname{asIso}(u_S)$ and $h=\operatorname{asIso}(u_I)$ whenever these augmentations are invertible. This definition supplies no invertibility assertion for either augmentation or for $\alpha_{v,h}$; its general interface retains the explicitly supplied $v,h$.
